questions.question: King Ajatashatru was a ruler of the ______ dynasty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **Haryanka ____**.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ajatashatru was one of the most important kings of the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha in East India.**
 
• He was the **son of King Bimbisara **and was a contemporary of **both Mahavira and Gautama Buddha.**
 
• He forcefully took over the kingdom of Magadha from his father and imprisoned him.
 
• **Pataliputra was founded by Udayin**, the son of the Haryanka king **Ajatashatru **in 490 BCE.
 
• Ajatashatru followed policies of conquest and expansion. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mauryan Dynasty**

 
 
• ​The Maurya Empire was **founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE.**
 
• The three great rulers of the Mauryan Empire were** ****Chandragupta Maurya****, Bindusara and Ashoka.**
 
 
 
• **​Shishunaga Dynasty​**
 
 
• **​Shishunaga (413 – 395 BCE) was the founder of the Shishunaga dynasty of the Magadha Empire** in present-day northern India.
 
• Initially, he was an amatya (official) of the Magadha Empire under the Haryanka dynasty. 
 
• Important rulers were Shishunaga, Kalashoka, and Nandivardhana.
 
 
 
• **Nanda Dynasty**
 
 
• **The most powerful ruler of the Nanda Dynasty is Mahapadma Nanda.**
 
• He was also the founder of the Nanda Dynasty.
 
• At the time of Alexander's invasion, Dhana Nand was the ruler of Magadha.
 
• Nanda Dynasty ruled in Magadha at the time of Alexander's invasion.
 
• The ruler was Dhana Nand, the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty.

questions.question: Capital of Ancient kingdom of Avanti was:
questions.solution:
The capital of the Ancient kingdom of Avanti was **Ujjain.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• In the sixth century BCE, Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, and Avanti were the most powerful states.
 
• The Vindhyas divided Avanti, into a northern and a southern portion, located in the Malwa area of central India. 
 
• The capital of this kingdom was both **Mahishmati**, which is now known as Maheshwar** and Ujjayini**, which is now close to Ujjain. Both of these places are mentioned in ancient writings as Avanti's capital
 
• Both the Deccan and ports on the western coast were connected to these two towns via key trade routes that ran through north India. Avanti had wars with the nations of Vatsa, Magadha, and Kosala under the rule of the illustrious monarch Pradyota.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Valabhi**, a city in ancient India, served as the Maitraka dynasty's capital from the fifth to the eighth centuries a.c.
 
• **Pataliputra **was the capital of the Magadhan Empire
 
• Sanchi is a significant stupa monument that unquestionably originates from the era of Ashoka (in Raisen district, MP). This was a location on the outskirts of ancient **Vidisha**, which was represented by the Besnagar site. According to Buddhist tradition, Devi, Ashoka's wife, was born in Vidisha, one of the main towns of his empire.

**Thus we know that the capital of the Ancient kingdom of Avanti was Ujjain.**

questions.question: Dilwara Temples in Mount Abu, Rajasthan, are associated with which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Jain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Dilwara Temples or Delvada Temples **are a collection of **svetambara Jain temples** situated in Sirohi District, Rajasthan's sole hill station, some** 212 kilometres from the Mount Abu town.**
 
• The **earliest were allegedly created **or at least funded by** Vastupala, **a Jain minister of **Dholka**, and were constructed by Bhima-1. Vastapul Tejpal, a minister for the** Bhima,Chalukyas of Gujrath king,** erected these Jain temples.
 
• Some experts also think that the **Dilwara Jain Temples is architecturally superior **to the Taj Mahal. It is one of the best Jain temples known around the world for its** amazing architecture **and magnificent marble stone carvings. 
 
• **Jains hold the same reincarnational beliefs** as Hindus and Buddhists. **One's karma** determines how often they will experience birth, death, and reincarnation. **Jains have the view that injuring living **creatures results in negative karma.
